title.narrative: Commercial Chamber Decisions Published on the Website

comment.narrative: <p>This objective has not been reached due to the skepticism of government teams regarding this practice. It has been widely documented in previous Aide-Mémoires. In response, the focus has been on the publication of business processing statistics at the Commercial Chamber level. These statistics can be found on the One Stop Shop Website and the 2017-2018 statistics have been annexed to the ICR. </p>

title.narrative: Adoption of legal and regulatory texts (new or revised) taken into account by the Doing Business report

comment.narrative: <p>The project supported the adoption of 10 laws pertaining to the improved business environment as planned. </p>

title.narrative: Magistrates trained in resolution of commercial disputes

comment.narrative: <p>All four magistrates specialized in that area have been trained. </p>
<p>All property titles have achieved a first level of digitization against 80 percent planned. They can be found through online search. </p>
<p>The final result at closing is almost double the initial target bringing a total increase of 67 percent of the registered businesses population. </p>

title.narrative: Avg. no of days to create a business

comment.narrative: <p>When the project was designed, the data source for this indicator was Doing Business report. According to the Doing Business report 2020, the current value of this indicator is 14 days. However, according the One-Stop-Shop statistical  report the maximum duration to create a business is 72 hours. The data challenges documents from the government explain this discrepancy as generated by the Doing Business methodology. The data was compiled from survey to Notaries who were referring to their historical practices and for Limited Companies which were not the subject of the intervention or the Doing Business data. </p>

title.narrative: Avg. no of days to register a

comment.narrative: <p>The average number to register a property decreased from 39 days to 24 days instead of the 10-day target. During the project implementation it has been highlighted that the initial target was too ambitious given the current state of the property registration system which was still manual. A study has been conducted in collaboration with the Urban GP and identified additional resources to support digitization in order to improve the quality of the service and accelerate the necessary checks by the administration and the notary. The activity is currently being undertaken under the additional financing of the Integrated Slum Upgrading Project. The " Djibouti Land Sector Review" report cited here is annexed. </p>

title.narrative: Transactions processed through the Automated Transfer System (ATS)

comment.narrative: <p>At completion,  the ATS + system is fully operational and supporting 90 percent of transactions. As of the November 2021, 100 percent of the transactions are supported by the system. </p>

title.narrative: Average Settlement time for credit transfers

comment.narrative: <p>The national payment system is operational and the average settling time for credit transfer successfully reached half a day as targeted. </p>

title.narrative: Users satisfied with the functioning of the One Stop Shop

comment.narrative: <p>The survey conducted in late 2019 has been annexed to the ICR.</p>

title.narrative: Establishment of primary data center for the national payment system

comment.narrative: <p>Despite delays of materials reception due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the data center has been  successfully set up for the NPS. </p>
